beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier moving through encode, window, repeated shared DQ-CTM ticks, and decode.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense spatial carrier from the compact process that updates it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing groups the feature field for local processing. The DQ-CTM thought process reads and updates those windows over repeated ticks. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into a super-resolved image. The ticks reuse the same DQ-CTM parameters instead of adding a new block each time.

params.headline: ThinkSR repeats one shared thought stage inside a dense image pipeline
params.note: The recurrence belongs to the DQ-CTM stage, not the whole flow.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first makes a dense feature field, then partitions that field into windows without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier starts as a dense feature field produced from the low-resolution input. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into that field. The window partition operates on the full field, so every token remains part of the computation.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first and partitioned second

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; at 1.129M parameters, it is second largest among the five methods.
beats.claim: Table 1 reports Params for CATANet 0.535M, RFDN 0.550M, IMDN 0.715M, DQ-CTM-SR 1.129M, and CARN 1.592M.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison does not make DQ-CTM-SR look cheap. CATANet is the smallest method in this table. RFDN is only slightly larger. IMDN sits in the middle of the group. DQ-CTM-SR is second largest at one point one two nine million parameters. CARN is the only method with more parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is second largest, not the cheapest model
